name: url-query
algorithm: Parse n generated application/x-www-form-urlencoded queries (splitmix64, seed 1; README.md states the generator), rounds times, with each language's standard query parser; about three pairs in four have nothing to decode, the rest hold '+' and escapes of whole UTF-8 sequences; no query holds ';' or a malformed escape, so the parsers give the same pairs; the checksum adds the length of every decoded name and value.

skip.c: no form-urlencoded parser in C's standard library
skip.rust: no form-urlencoded parser in Rust's std (form_urlencoded is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.zig: no form-urlencoded parser in Zig's std (std.Uri splits a URL but does not parse a query's pairs)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the parser is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdUrl_QueryModel, TestStdUrl_ParseQueryAgainstGo, FuzzStdUrl_ParseQuery)
notes: Mk: url.ParseQuery, the URL Standard's section 5.1, into a fresh arena each round, freed at its end (no warm memory, as std-encoding's finding F5 asks); a pair with nothing to decode is one copy of its bytes, any other is decoded into a buffer of its length and checked as UTF-8, and the pairs are a List in the arena. Go: net/url.ParseQuery, a map from name to values, with a string returned as it is when it has nothing to decode.
Added for the std-url review's finding url-03 (2026-11-13). Checksums agree between Go and Mk at the quick and publish sizes on the owner's machine (Go 1.27, mk from the tree).
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
